research_notes: Long-run useful utilization can be modeled as successful useful work divided by wall time including relay gaps and failed-run losses.
This metric naturally penalizes overly aggressive caps that increase termination risk.
It also penalizes overly conservative caps that create excessive handoff frequency and idle gaps.
The optimal operating point is therefore expected below the absolute observed survival maximum.
Gap optimization and parallelism can later shift that optimum by reducing idle wall time.
Those later improvements should preserve the runtime safety envelope established first.
